name: 中華そば まる 舟入店 (Chuka Soba Maru Funairi-ten)

claims.text: The broth and seasoning are soy-sauce based; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and the noodles are wheat noodles.
Pork-bone broth and pork chashu are central to the menu; all dishes share this meat-based broth.

name: 中華そば 寿々女 (Chuka Soba Suzume)

claims.text: The broth is described as a soy-sauce pork-bone (醤油豚骨) base characteristic of Hiroshima ramen; standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat.
Core dishes are pork-based ramen and braised-pork rice in animal broth; no vegetarian or vegan preparation is documented.

name: 中華そば つばめ (Chuka Soba Tsubame)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles and a wheat-containing soy-sauce broth are central to the menu, and oden shares the same soy-based stock, so gluten is pervasive throughout the kitchen.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base, which in standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Broth is pork-bone based with pork chashu, and oden uses the same animal stock and fish-based items, so no dishes are free of animal products.

name: 中華そば うぐいす (Chuka Soba Uguisu)

claims.text: Single tiny counter kitchen built entirely around wheat ramen noodles and shared soy-sauce broth; no separation possible.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) tonkotsu base; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat.
Pork-bone broth and chashu pork are the foundation of the dish; oden uses fish/meat dashi. No vegan preparation exists.

name: 中華そば 陽気 大手町店 (Chuka Soba Youki Otemachi-ten)

claims.text: The single dish is wheat ramen noodles cooked in shared boiling water; no gluten-free preparation exists.
The broth is finished with a soy-sauce-based tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The broth is simmered from pork bones, chicken bones and vegetables, so it is animal-based and not separable for vegan diners.
The shop is a single-griddle teppan okonomiyaki counter where wheat batter and wheat noodles are cooked on the same surface, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent.
Okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki/soy-based sauce, which is wheat-based; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
The shared griddle cooks pork, squid, shrimp and egg, so any item would have animal cross-contact.

name: DASHIとSOBA 水車 (DASHI to SOBA Suisha)

claims.text: Sarashina-style soba noodles are made from buckwheat blended with wheat flour and are boiled in shared water; no gluten-free noodle or dedicated pot is documented.
The regular dashi/tare is finished with soy sauce and the kitchen runs multiple soy-based stocks (soba-gaeshi, don-gaeshi, etc.); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

The plant-based dashi is animal-free, but it is prepared in the same kitchen that runs bonito-based broths and shared noodle-boiling water; no separate-equipment or cross-contact protocol is published.
Only general guidance is given: bringing homemade food for infants/preschoolers with allergies is allowed with prior consultation; no allergen chart or formal allergy-handling protocol is published.

Offers a dedicated, staff-developed plant-based (vegan) soba using a kombu-shiitake-vegetable dashi with no animal ingredients, explicitly aimed at guests who cannot eat animal products and at international visitors.
The plant-based menu is described as halal-conscious ('ハラール対応'), though no formal halal certification is documented.
The signature dish is glazed with a house tare/sauce that is soy-sauce based, which conventionally contains wheat; no wheat-free version is documented.
The kitchen is built around conger eel and a fish/dashi-and-soy sauce; the rice itself is dressed with this sauce, so it is not suitable for vegans and there is no documented plant-based dish.
